besselDomainArgument.derivation: Differentiate the Sturm equation in lambda for u(r)=J_nu(lambda*r). Lagrange identity gives [r(v*uprime-u*vprime)]_0^1=2lambda integral(r*u^2). The defining series makes the zero endpoint vanish. At a root, v(1)=Jprime(alpha), uprime(1)=alpha*Jprime(alpha); division gives integral=Jprime(alpha)^2/2=J_(nu+1)(alpha)^2/2.
besselDomainArgument.rootDomain: For nu>=1 and0<z<=2, the normalized alternating series exceeds1-z²/[4(nu+1)]>=nu/(nu+1)>0. For nu=0 the first pair is positive for z<2; at z=2 the next pair1/4-1/36>0 and the remaining alternating tail is positive. Thus alpha>2. Coefficient ratios decrease, justifying each bound.
besselDomainArgument.positiveScale: At alpha>0 the ODE is regular. A common zero of J_nu and J_(nu+1) would also have derivative zero by the coefficient-checked recurrence, contradicting uniqueness and the nonzero defining series. Hence B=J_(nu+1)(alpha)^2>0.
